institutionName: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses at NKUA and the cultural and historical heritage of Athens.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was as expected.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an intro meeting online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, but you have to be aware of scammers. I used facebook and airbnb and was able to find a really nice place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have to be very aware of which area you choose to live in, as some can be rather uncomfortable especially if you are a female. I would avoid Omonia and Bictoria but i knew a lot of students who lived there, and liked it so it depends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know because i didnt look into it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We got minimal information about this. I had no idea if i was registered on any courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was non. You just got a schedule and show up to the classes you want to follow and the exam.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had chosen a course in my learning agreement which was supposed to have a written exam and essay and classes 4 hours a week for 9 ECTS. This was changed to only an essay, no classes or written exam for 6 ECTS, whiteouts any information given to the students. Because of this i was forced to change my learning agreement last minute and i also didn't receive education in this course as expected, since i only had to write an essay. I found this to be particularly unorganized but other than that i was able to go to the classes i wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not like you are used to. Just go to class whit out registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the educators where very dedicated but the level was lower than i am used to. However it was a fair level and not too easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A particular difference is, that we didn't have any written material that we could read before class in order to prepare. This made it difficult to have a discussion in class. Also the facilities are a lot different and there is graffiti and political posters all over the school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Maritime law 
Intellectual property law 
EU-law 
International telecommunications law 
Competition law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Intellectual property law
Maritime law

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of social events and trips every week that Erasmus students could participate in in Athens, both connected to NKUA and the other universities in Athens.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mykonos and Santorini trip

questions.answer:
Island hopping
Smut club

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I fit right in. Loved the Greek mentality.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The lifestyle, particularly going out a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Research the area before you choose an apartment
Take more courses instead of writing many essays - they often require between 15-20 pages  
Take advantage of the cheap ferries to nearby islands

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The coordinator Maria Parara is really helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many amazing people and experiencing living in a very different city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it challenging at all.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Athens is amazing i would recommend anyone to do exchange here.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
